# Market Intel

> Prediction-market microstructure, measured on Polymarket and Kalshi order
> books this project recorded itself. Every figure on the site carries its
> sample size, its interval where one can be computed, and the timestamp of
> the file it came from. Results that came out negative are published as they
> are.

Research tool only: no investment advice, no order placement, no venue affiliation. Public Polymarket and Kalshi data, provided as-is.

## What this site is

A read-only research terminal and the studies it runs on. No order path exists
in the codebase, and the authenticated Kalshi socket signs GET requests only.
The interactive terminal needs a wide screen; a narrow device gets a readable
summary instead.

Nothing here forecasts a market or recommends a position. The wallet pages
describe what a public address did in the past, counted per event over settled
positions only, and state when the sample is too small to carry a verdict.

## Where the findings are

- Frozen microstructure studies (order-book imbalance, order flow net of
  costs, market-making decomposition, cross-venue gaps, gap lifetime, reward
  pools, resolution rules, book reconciliation): /#research/microstructure
- How the studies are measured, and how a wallet record is counted:
  /#research/methodology
- Small-stake live runs and the pre-registered pilot: /#research/live-runs and
  /#research/pilot
- Post-mortems of incidents that cost money or data: /#research/post-mortems
- Field notes from the tape: /#research/field-notes

Every study card links its full report, the module that computed it, and the
dataset behind it, all in the public repository.

## Where the data is

The research payloads are published as JSON under /data/ and are the same
files the pages read; the site works from a plain file server without an API.
The live market pages need the JSON API and show a named empty state without
it.

## Source

Code, reports and datasets: https://github.com/Pablozh123/prediction-market-terminal

Legal and contact: /imprint.html, /privacy.html,
/.well-known/security.txt

## How to cite what you find here

Name the study, the payload timestamp shown beside the figure, and the sample
size. A figure quoted without its n and its interval says less than it looks
like it says, which is the whole point of the way this site is written.
